logp.method_description: Partition coefficients of the platinum(II) complexes were determined in the octanol/water system. Briefly, platinum complexes were dissolved and diluted to 50 μM in water. Equal volumes of the drug solution and n-octanol were shaken in vortex for 15 min, and after centrifugation (4000 rpm for 15 min) the platinum content in the aqueous layers was analyzed by ICP-AES. The partition coefficient (P) is expressed as P=[Pt]o/[Pt]w, where [Pt]o and [Pt]w represent the total concentrations of the complex in the n-octanol and water layers, respectively, and the lipophilicity may be defined as its log function (log P). Thus the measured lipophilicities of the platinum(II) complexes are listed in Table 1. The lipophilicity of the complexes was plotted against the number of carbon atoms (n) of the N-substituents of the amino acids in Fig. 2. The n values of complexes 1–4 are 2, 3, 5 and 8, respectively, which are corresponding to the number of carbon atoms of Ac, Pro, Piv and Cbz groups, respectively.
